cells.why: the resumed batch no longer says whose it is: the server can replay it but cannot bind it to the interrupted round, which is the half this order was opened for
the ruling's 'two keys, never merged' violated in the direction that looks harmless: one name standing in for both, so 'same mission, different request' and 'same request, resent' collapse in storage

clause 5's forbidden shape -- the record is erased AHEAD of the send, so a run interrupted after this press is unfindable again. (v1 measured this arm with a different edit: moving the post-await clear out of its condition still erased after the send, which is a different defect and cell 1 correctly ignored it. That mutant was wrong, not the gate.)
a refusal, timeout or dead transport paints no word and leaves the card standing -- the 'never silence' half of the reveal
the pre-fix shape: the leg the server actually reads arrives with no identity, so the receipt machinery never sees the phone's own press
only one leg of one press carries the identity, so the two disagree about whose send this is -- 'one intent, one key' broken across the legs rather than dropped from both
the key stops being per intent and becomes a per-session constant: both legs still agree, so only the second-press node can see it -- which is what that node exists for
